title: Germany's Fragile Recovery: Growth Returns · 21 Oct
keywords: Germany, economic recovery, AfD, Alternative für Deutschland, inflation, energy prices, investor confidence, ZEW index, Friedrich Merz, EU economy, political polarisation, cost of living, foreign investment, skilled labour, GDP growth
notes: Germany's government has upgraded its growth forecast for 2026, citing stronger exports and public investment, but persistently high inflation and energy costs are limiting what citizens feel in their daily lives. At the same time, rising support for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland is increasingly framed not only as a political challenge but as a risk to investment and long-term economic stability. The gap between official optimism and lived experience is at the heart of both debates.
